Systemic `!!` non-null assertions on nullable UI-state properties across the Compose androidApp: ListingDetailScreen.kt:121,125,132,149,160 (`state.errorMessage!!`, `state.listing!!` from `viewModel.state.collectAsState()`); InquiriesScreen.kt:169 (`errorMessage!!` from a local `var by remember { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }`); FavoritesScreen.kt:164 (same pattern); AccountScreen.kt:174 (`notificationPrefs!!` inside `if (notificationsExpanded && notificationPrefs != null)`). Kotlin cannot smart-cast a property getter on `state` nor a delegated `var`, so the branch guard does not imply non-null at the use site.

The pattern is a latent crash class: while Compose's snapshot system usually keeps reads within one composition consistent, any state update between the null-check condition evaluation and the argument-list evaluation (e.g. the ViewModel's StateFlow emitting from a coroutine mid-composition, or a `LaunchedEffect` in a sibling branch mutating the local `errorMessage` state) will throw KotlinNullPointerException. This is the exact category of bug that killed VoteDetailScreen (see the neighbour segment's 2026-08-23 finding on Rules of Hooks) — silent-until-it-crashes state-management fragility.

Idiomatic fix mirrors how the same file already gates other branches: capture the value into a local val at the top of the `when` branch, e.g. `state.listing != null -> { val listing = state.listing; ... ListingContent(listing = listing, ...) }` or use `state.listing?.let { listing -> ... } ?: return`. The FavoritesScreen retry lambda demonstrates the safer style with `.fold(onSuccess = { ... })`. Applying the fix removes the `!!` and lets the compiler enforce the invariant.

backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/sso.rs:687, :711, :748 — the three PM-OAuth helper fns exchange_pm_token (687), get_user_info (711) and introspect_pm_token (748) each build a fresh `reqwest::Client::new()` with NO `.timeout(...)`. reqwest's default client has no request timeout, so a slow/hung PM OAuth server leaves the awaiting reality-server task blocked indefinitely — tasks and their held DB/socket resources pile up → resource-exhaustion / cascading unavailability on the reality-server process.

This path is reachable from PUBLIC/unauthenticated SSO entry points: introspect_pm_token is invoked at sso.rs:417 (POST /api/v1/sso/exchange), :899 and :1073 (session-sync), and get_user_info at :270/:434/:917/:1109 on the OAuth callback path. A browser/attacker can drive these endpoints, so a degraded PM API turns into a reality-server outage with no upper bound on wait time.

The codebase already knows to bound these calls: state.rs:754-762 (PmApiClient::new, Story 104.1) builds its reqwest client via `Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(timeout_seconds)).build()`. The SSO OAuth helpers bypass that shared, timeout-configured client and construct raw per-call clients instead — which additionally defeats connection pooling / keep-alive to the PM API on the per-request introspection hot path (only 60s-cached via token_cache). Fix: route these calls through a shared `reqwest::Client` built with an explicit timeout (mirror PmApiClient), or add `.timeout(...)` + reuse one client stored on AppState.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:659 — the `Matches` comparison operator calls `regex::Regex::new(pattern)` on every single workflow condition evaluation. `pattern` is `compare_value.as_str()`, i.e. an org-authored stored workflow condition. grep of the file finds exactly one `Regex::new` and no `Lazy`/`OnceCell`/cache, so the pattern is recompiled from scratch for every event that reaches the condition.

Cost/DoS amplification on a hot automation path: a workflow bound to a high-frequency event type (e.g. a per-notification or per-fault trigger) recompiles its regex on each matching event. A workflow author can also store an expensive-to-compile pattern (the crate's default 10MB compiled-size ceiling is large) that is paid on every evaluation rather than once. Fix: compile once and cache (e.g. an LRU/`OnceCell` keyed by pattern) and/or set an explicit `RegexBuilder::size_limit`.

Confidence medium: static read confirms the recompile-per-eval and absence of any cache; the reachability (event -> evaluate_condition -> Matches) is via the stored-condition path and not runtime-confirmed for frequency.

backend/servers/api-server/src/services/workflow_executor.rs:640-652 — `ComparisonOperator::In` returns `Ok(false)` when `compare_value.as_array()` is `None` (fails closed), but `ComparisonOperator::NotIn` returns `Ok(true)` in the same malformed case (fails open).

Effect: a workflow condition authored as `NotIn` whose value is mis-typed (object/string/number instead of a JSON array) silently matches every event and fires the workflow's downstream actions, with no error surfaced to the author (contrast `Matches`, which returns a `ConditionError` on a non-string pattern). Recommend returning a `WorkflowError::ConditionError` for a non-array `In`/`NotIn` value so a malformed condition is rejected rather than firing unintentionally.
Confidence medium: asymmetry is clear from the source; whether a mis-typed `NotIn` config can actually be persisted depends on upstream config validation not traced in this static pass.

Fix: guard the drainer behind real transports (or keep SEARCH_ALERT_DRAINER_ENABLED=false in prod until an adapter exists) so it does not consume/mark-delivered rows it cannot actually deliver.
